policy: A founding relation needs evidence of the journal’s constitutive role in an emerging field or school. A launch mission or later consolidation alone is insufficient. Title histories are separate bibliography.

edge.relationship: Launched in 1995 to broaden environmental history’s geographical and disciplinary conversation, including work on Africa, Asia and other regions alongside Europe and North America.
edge.evidence_note: An expansion and consolidation project in an already established field. Its explicit geographical ambitions provide evidence against treating North American environmental-history venues as the field’s whole institutional history.

withdrawals.reason: User correction confirmed by Grove’s 1995 editorial: Environment and History complements an already existing field and its journals. It is not the field-forming journal requested. Replaced by Environmental Review (1976), linked to the institutional emergence of US environmental history.

added_sources.title: American Society for Environmental History, History of ASEH
added_sources.note: Institutional history read: joint journal/association organizing effort in 1976, journal launch in 1976 and society formation in 1977. Evidence of field-building, not merely a publisher remit. Earlier intellectual roots and traditions outside the US are not erased.

added_sources.title: JSTOR, Environmental History: title history
added_sources.note: User-supplied page and complete-title-history export checked. Family contains overlapping environmental and forest-history branches, not one succession chain. added_sources.title: Oxford Academic, Environmental History Review: About the Journal
added_sources.note: Publisher record read: Environmental Review 1976–1989 continues as Environmental History Review 1990–1995, which merges with Forest & Conservation History in 1996 to form Environmental History. The archive’s 2006 endpoint is not cessation.

added_edges.relationship: Launched in 1976 as part of the organizing effort that established an institutional community for environmental history in the United States and produced ASEH in 1977.
added_edges.evidence_note: The journal and society were planned together to organize an emerging field. This institutional formation is distinct from the later 1990 renaming, 1996 merger and the separate Environment and History launched in 1995. It does not make US institutionalization the origin of all environmental historical thought.

added_title_relationships.evidence_note: Continuation within the forest-history branch, separately from Environmental Review.

before.title: Richard Grove, Editorial, Environment and History 1(1) (1995), 1–2
before.note: Complete two-page founding editorial read. Describes planning with Ramachandra Guha, connections to history from below and material culture, and a geographically broad programme complementing existing North American venues. An incidental erroneous Silent Spring date is not used.
